text:
sara_marketing: Heads up — working on the webinar slide deck and we need a final sanity run for the launch benchmarks. Can eng/runtime help with a rerun and a short methodology note we can quote? Ideally need P95 latency, cost-per-1k tokens, and 5 sample outputs for quantized vs fp16 that we can include. Target: tomorrow EOD. @josh_runtime @lee_runtime :pray:

josh_runtime: Sure — can you confirm the exact model/artifact, dataset slice, and traffic profile? Also do you want cold-starts included or just steady-state?

sara_marketing: Model: redwood-1.3b (verified tag v2.1). Dataset: the demo seeded sample (500 prompts, seed id: demo-seed-2026). Traffic: steady 50 rps with a 1-minute spike to 200 rps. Please include warm and cold start snapshots and a short representative output set.

lee_runtime: We can run that. Need to confirm quant variants: int8 (8-bit), int4 (4-bit), and fp16? Also confirm batching and concurrency. Our current bench defaults are batch_size=8 and max_concurrency=32. Will that match marketing expectations for the 'production-like' numbers?

sara_marketing: Yes to int8, int4, and fp16. Keep default batching for the production-like run, but please also add batch_size=1 for an "interactive" latency view. Add a 2-line methodology blurb we can paste in slides (warmup policy, which metrics we report, and how cost is estimated).

josh_runtime: Got it. Plan: run three configs (fp16,int8,int4) x two batch sizes (1,8). We'll capture p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm p95, GPU-seconds -> $ cost estimate using current instance pricing, and 5 representative outputs per config. Expected runtime ~2h. If variance >20% we'll rerun. Any objections @olivia_p?

olivia_p: Sounds good. Marketing wants the exact commit/model artifact hash in the methodology note (so we can footnote reproducibility).

sara_marketing: Perfect. Also include the short methodology blurb draft: "Runs used N warmup requests; metrics computed on the subsequent M requests; cost estimated from GPU-second pricing snapshot on the run date." Feel free to rewrite for clarity.

lee_runtime: We'll include that and the artifact hash. Command we'll run for reproducibility:
```
bench-run --model redwood-1.3b:v2.1 --prompts demo-seed-2026.json --configs fp16,int8,int4 --batch-sizes 1,8 --rps-profile steady:50,spike:200 --out results/2460012345/
```
We'll attach raw logs, the small CSV of latency buckets, and 5 sample outputs per config in results/. If int4 shows instability we'll document it and include a note about extra warmup.

bench-bot: Run started on infra cluster-6. Job ID: run-2460012345. ETA ~2h.

sara_marketing: :thumbsup: Thanks — can you ping here when complete with the short blurb and the top-line numbers so we can update the slides? If anything changes on scope, call it out.

josh_runtime: Will do. Quick heads-up: if the int4 path hits thermal/throughput fallback we'll note the failure mode and include fallback numbers. ETA updated ~2.5h.

bench-bot: Run update: int4 config completed warmup phase and is at ~35% of sample processing. No errors so far.

lee_runtime: For the cost calc we'll use $3.20/hr as our A40-equivalent price (compute) + an amortized infra fee. We'll include the exact formula in the methodology note so marketing can reproduce the $/1k-token number.

sara_marketing: Thanks team. If you can include one short marketing-friendly sentence we can drop into the deck: "Redwood delivers consistent P95 latency under X ms at 50 rps while reducing token cost by Y% with quantized models." We'll fill X/Y after runs.

josh_runtime: Copy. We'll post top-line numbers (p95, cost delta vs fp16) + the methodology blurb and artifact hash in this thread when the run finishes.
